developer_request: This project has several repositories, status documents, old branches, and draft ideas. Understand what is actually current and continue from the right place.
known_facts: Different repositories own different layers of authority.
Merged content may still be Draft/Proposed rather than accepted authority.
Open or historical branches can be materially behind the current product baseline.
The next useful change should follow the current source of truth rather than whichever artifact is easiest to find.
expected_first_moves: identify scoped instruction and current-fact sources before broad code reading
record source authority and freshness for material claims
separate current, draft/proposed, historical, and unknown evidence
choose one highest-leverage current blocker only after reconciling contradictory sources
must_not: treat merge-to-main as proof that a document is accepted/stable authority
pick the newest-looking file as truth without checking its declared role
start broad cleanup before reconstructing current state
promote product-specific behavior into a shared protocol merely because it exists
lessons: Repository recovery needs evidence authority and temporal status, not only file inventory.
Conflicts should be preserved and reconciled instead of silently choosing a winner.
Current-fact source selection is an engineering decision that can change the entire route.
